warnings: This experiment uses FIVE CO2 levels (300, 450, 600, 750, 900 ppm), not just one elevated vs one control. The 'control' is 300 ppm, which is below ambient (pre-industrial level), not the typical ~380 ppm ambient. This is unusual and must be noted.

The study design means multiple pairwise comparisons are possible. For meta-analysis purposes, the most relevant elevated CO2 level should be selected (likely 600 or 750 ppm as closest to typical FACE/OTC elevated levels).

Three leaf age classes are reported separately (young, completely expanded, old leaves) - each represents a different biological unit and should be extracted separately or the most relevant class chosen.
The 300 ppm 'control' is below current ambient CO2, so effect sizes relative to this control will be larger than typical meta-analyses using ~380 ppm as control.
Macronutrient data are reported per leaf age class - ensure correct age class is matched to correct CO2 treatment row.
Significant differences are indicated by letters within columns - ensure letter comparisons are made within the correct leaf age group and column.

recon.treatment_definition: Elevated CO2 at 450, 600, 750, or 900 ppm (±20 ppm)
recon.potential_tc_confusion: The control (300 ppm) is below current ambient (~400 ppm), not a typical ambient control. This could inflate apparent dilution effects compared to meta-analyses using ~380 ppm as control. Also, 450 ppm could be considered close to current ambient, making it a possible alternative reference point.
recon.sample_size_source: From the five samples per variant, three were randomly selected to determine macronutrient and carbohydrate contents.
recon.factorial_structure: ["CO2 concentration (5 levels)", "leaf age class (3 levels: young, completely expanded, old)"]
recon.extraction_guidance: Extract mineral data from Table 3 only. For each mineral (N, P, K, Ca, Mg), extract data separately for each of the three leaf age classes (young, completely expanded, old). Control = 300 ppm CO2 row; choose the most relevant elevated CO2 level for the meta-analysis (600 ppm is closest to typical FACE elevated; 750 ppm is also commonly used). Units are mg/g dry matter. n=3 for all nutrient measurements. SD is the variance measure. Be aware that 300 ppm control is sub-ambient - flag this in extraction. Chl in Table 3 is not a mineral element and should not be extracted as a primary mineral outcome. The paper reports no Fe, Zn, Mn, Cu, or other micronutrients - only the five macronutrients listed. For the meta-analysis comparison, the most defensible pairing is 300 ppm (control) vs 600 ppm (closest to typical elevated treatment in literature), but 750 or 900 ppm pairings are also extractable.

table_descriptions.Table 2: Chlorophyll fluorescence parameters: Fo, Fm, Fv/Fm, actual quantum yield (delta F/Fm'), qN, qP for three leaf age classes at five CO2 concentrations
table_descriptions.Table 3: Macronutrient contents (N, P, K, Ca, Mg) and total chlorophyll (Chl) in mg/g dry matter for three leaf age classes at five CO2 concentrations - PRIMARY OUTCOME TABLE
table_descriptions.Table 4: Carbohydrate contents (starch, glucose, fructose, sucrose, total carbohydrate) in % dry matter for three leaf age classes at five CO2 concentrations
